blocks.en: Radical Trust · "Even the Wind and the Waves Obey Him" (Mark 4:41)
blocks.es_reference: Confianza Radical · "Aun el Viento y las Olas le Obedecen" (Mr 4:41)

blocks.en: Course Author: Dr. Wayne Cook · Chapala Theological Seminary
blocks.es_reference: Autor del Curso: Dr. Wayne Cook · Seminario Teológico de Chapala

blocks.en: When Jesus said, "No one pours new wine into old wineskins" (Luke 5:37-38), He was describing the radical life He brings. New wine ferments and expands; old, brittle wineskins burst under the pressure. New wineskins, though, stretch to hold the new wine. In the same way, Jesus calls His disciples into a faith that stretches us beyond what feels safe or comfortable — the kind of trust that does not collapse under storms, worries, or uncertainty. There are three places this trust gets stretched: over storms, over worry, and over what the eye cannot yet see.
blocks.es_reference: Cuando Jesús dijo, "Nadie echa vino nuevo en odres viejos" (Lucas 5:37-38), estaba describiendo la vida radical que Él trae. El vino nuevo fermenta y se expande; los odres viejos y frágiles revientan bajo la presión. Los odres nuevos, sin embargo, se estiran para contener el vino nuevo. De la misma manera, Jesús llama a Sus discípulos a una fe que los estire más allá de lo que se siente seguro o cómodo — la clase de confianza que no se colapsa bajo tormentas, preocupaciones, o incertidumbre. Hay tres lugares donde esta confianza se estira: sobre las tormentas, sobre la preocupación, y sobre lo que el ojo aún no puede ver.

blocks.en: 1. The Lord Over Storms
blocks.es_reference: 1. El Señor Sobre las Tormentas

blocks.en: Mark 4:37-41 (NKJV) — abridged: "And a great windstorm arose, and the waves beat into the boat, so that it was already filling. But He was in the stern, asleep on a pillow. And they awoke Him and said to Him, 'Teacher, do You not care that we are perishing?' Then He arose and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, 'Peace, be still!' And the wind ceased and there was a great calm… And they feared exceedingly, and said to one another, 'Who can this be, that even the wind and the sea obey Him!'"
blocks.es_reference: Marcos 4:37-41 (RVG) — abreviado: "Y se levantó una gran tempestad de viento, y las olas batían contra la barca, de modo que ya se llenaba. Y Él estaba en la popa, durmiendo sobre un cabezal; y le despertaron, y le dijeron: Maestro, ¿no tienes cuidado que perecemos? Y levantándose, reprendió al viento, y dijo al mar: ¡Calla, enmudece! Y cesó el viento, y se hizo grande bonanza… Y temieron con gran temor, y se decían el uno al otro: ¿Quién es Éste, que aun el viento y el mar le obedecen?"

blocks.en: Jesus asked the disciples to cross the Sea of Galilee, and a storm broke out so fierce that the boat began filling with water. These were not weekend sailors; several of them were professional fishermen. They had handled bad weather before. This storm scared them. And where was Jesus while they were terrified? Asleep in the stern, with His head on a cushion. They shook Him awake with what is half-accusation, half-prayer: Teacher, do You not care that we are perishing? Jesus stood up, rebuked the wind, and said three words to the sea: Peace, be still. The wind ceased. The water flattened. And the men who had been afraid of the storm now had something larger to be afraid of, because the One in the boat with them commanded weather.
blocks.es_reference: Jesús pidió a los discípulos cruzar el Mar de Galilea, y se desató una tormenta tan feroz que la barca comenzó a llenarse de agua. Estos no eran marineros de fin de semana; varios de ellos eran pescadores profesionales. Habían manejado mal clima antes. Esta tormenta los asustó. ¿Y dónde estaba Jesús mientras ellos estaban aterrorizados? Dormido en la popa, con la cabeza sobre un cabezal. Lo despertaron sacudiéndolo con lo que es mitad acusación, mitad oración: Maestro, ¿no tienes cuidado que perecemos? Jesús se levantó, reprendió al viento, y dijo tres palabras al mar: Calla, enmudece. El viento cesó. El agua se aplanó. Y los hombres que habían tenido miedo de la tormenta ahora tenían algo más grande de qué tener miedo, porque Aquel que estaba en la barca con ellos mandaba el clima.

blocks.en: The lesson is not that storms will never come; the lesson is that the Lord of the storm is in the boat with you. Radical trust does not deny the weather; it knows who is sleeping on the cushion. Faith does not always stop the storm, but it anchors the disciple to the Savior who rules over it. The disciples' question — do You not care? — is the question every storm draws out of every Christian eventually, and the answer is the same answer Jesus gave them: He cares enough to be in the boat, and He has authority enough to make the wind listen.
blocks.es_reference: La lección no es que las tormentas nunca vendrán; la lección es que el Señor de la tormenta está en la barca contigo. La confianza radical no niega el clima; sabe quién está durmiendo sobre el cabezal. La fe no siempre detiene la tormenta, pero ancla al discípulo al Salvador que la gobierna. La pregunta de los discípulos — ¿no tienes cuidado? — es la pregunta que cada tormenta saca de cada cristiano eventualmente, y la respuesta es la misma respuesta que Jesús les dio: Él tiene suficiente cuidado para estar en la barca, y tiene suficiente autoridad para hacer que el viento escuche.

blocks.en: Elisabeth Elliot: In 1956, five young missionaries in Ecuador set out to reach the Huaorani tribe. The Huaorani attacked, and all five were speared to death. Jim Elliot's wife, Elisabeth, was twenty-nine, with a baby daughter. Two years later, she went to live among the very tribe that had killed her husband. She showed them Christ's love. In time, many Huaorani came to faith, including some of the men who had wielded the spears. The same Jesus who stilled the Sea of Galilee still rules over life's fiercest storms.
blocks.es_reference: Elisabeth Elliot: En 1956, cinco jóvenes misioneros en Ecuador salieron a alcanzar a la tribu Huaorani. Los Huaorani los atacaron, y los cinco fueron muertos con lanzas. La esposa de Jim Elliot, Elisabeth, tenía veintinueve años, con una bebé. Dos años después, fue a vivir entre la misma tribu que había matado a su esposo. Les mostró el amor de Cristo. Con el tiempo, muchos Huaorani vinieron a la fe, incluyendo algunos de los hombres que habían blandido las lanzas. El mismo Jesús que calmó el Mar de Galilea aún gobierna sobre las tormentas más feroces de la vida.

blocks.en: Application is direct. When the storm comes — and it will come — the disciple's first response is not panic but prayer. The disciple says, Jesus is in my boat. He may not calm this storm tonight. He may calm it tomorrow. He may not calm it at all and instead carry the disciple through the middle of it. None of these outcomes is a sign that He does not care. All three are a sign that He is sovereign and present. The radical disciple's posture toward storms is therefore not desperation but rest — the rest of someone who knows the One who is sleeping with His head on the cushion is the same One who made the wind.
blocks.es_reference: La aplicación es directa. Cuando venga la tormenta — y vendrá — la primera respuesta del discípulo no es el pánico sino la oración. El discípulo dice, Jesús está en mi barca. Puede que no calme esta tormenta esta noche. Puede que la calme mañana. Puede que no la calme en absoluto y en cambio lleve al discípulo a través del medio de ella. Ninguno de estos resultados es señal de que Él no tiene cuidado. Los tres son señal de que Él es soberano y presente. La postura del discípulo radical hacia las tormentas no es por tanto desesperación sino descanso — el descanso de alguien que sabe que Aquel que está durmiendo con la cabeza sobre el cabezal es el mismo que hizo el viento.

blocks.en: 2. The Lord Over Worry
blocks.es_reference: 2. El Señor Sobre la Preocupación

blocks.en: Matthew 6:25-27, 33 (NKJV) — abridged: "Therefore I say to you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat or what you will drink; nor about your body, what you will put on… Look at the birds of the air, for they neither sow nor reap nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not of more value than they? Which of you by worrying can add one cubit to his stature?… But seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things shall be added to you."
blocks.es_reference: Mateo 6:25-27, 33 (RVG) — abreviado: "Por tanto os digo: No os afanéis por vuestra vida, qué habéis de comer, o qué habéis de beber; ni por vuestro cuerpo, qué habéis de vestir… Mirad las aves del cielo, que no siembran, ni siegan, ni recogen en graneros; y vuestro Padre celestial las alimenta. ¿No sois vosotros mucho mejores que ellas? ¿Quién de vosotros podrá, por mucho que se afane, añadir a su estatura un codo?… Mas buscad primeramente el reino de Dios y su justicia, y todas estas cosas os serán añadidas."

blocks.en: If the storm chapter is about the great fears, the worry chapter is about the small ones — food, drink, clothing, the bills that did not stop coming when the paycheck did. Jesus addresses these directly. He points the disciples to two ordinary things in front of them. Birds do not run agribusiness; they have no granaries; the Father feeds them anyway. Lilies do not weave fabric; they have no looms; Solomon in his full royal wardrobe was not as well dressed as the wildflower that comes up in three weeks and is gone in six. The argument is not that food and clothing do not matter. The argument is that they matter to the Father.
blocks.es_reference: Si el capítulo de la tormenta es sobre los grandes temores, el capítulo de la preocupación es sobre los pequeños — comida, bebida, ropa, las cuentas que no dejaron de venir cuando el sueldo se acabó. Jesús los aborda directamente. Apunta a los discípulos a dos cosas ordinarias frente a ellos. Las aves no manejan agronegocios; no tienen graneros; el Padre las alimenta de todos modos. Los lirios no tejen telas; no tienen telares; Salomón en su completo vestuario real no estaba tan bien vestido como la flor silvestre que sale en tres semanas y se va en seis. El argumento no es que la comida y la ropa no importan. El argumento es que le importan al Padre.

blocks.en: Then Jesus asks a question that should embarrass every Christian who has lain awake at three in the morning: Which of you by worrying can add one cubit to his stature? The honest answer is none. Worry has never lengthened a life, paid a bill, healed a child, or restored a marriage. What worry actually does is impersonate prayer while accomplishing none of prayer's work. It feels like spiritual labor and produces only fatigue. The disciple's alternative is named in verse 33: seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things shall be added to you. The order matters. The kingdom is first; the needs come after. Reverse the order and even the needs do not get met properly.
blocks.es_reference: Luego Jesús hace una pregunta que debería avergonzar a cada cristiano que ha estado despierto a las tres de la mañana: ¿quién de vosotros podrá, por mucho que se afane, añadir a su estatura un codo? La respuesta honesta es ninguno. La preocupación nunca ha alargado una vida, pagado una cuenta, sanado a un niño, o restaurado un matrimonio. Lo que la preocupación realmente hace es imitar la oración mientras no logra nada del trabajo de la oración. Se siente como labor espiritual y produce solo fatiga. La alternativa del discípulo se nombra en el versículo 33: buscad primeramente el reino de Dios y su justicia, y todas estas cosas os serán añadidas. El orden importa. El reino es primero; las necesidades vienen después. Invierte el orden y aun las necesidades no son satisfechas apropiadamente.

blocks.en: Linda's Empty Fridge: During the 2009 financial crisis, a single mother in Ohio named Linda lost her job. Her refrigerator was nearly empty. After tucking her three children into bed she broke down in the kitchen and prayed, Lord, I don't know how we'll eat tomorrow. But You promised to care for us. I trust You. The next morning a friend from church knocked at the door with bags of groceries. The friend said, I couldn't sleep last night — I felt God telling me you needed this. Linda's testimony afterward was not about the food; it was that God already knew what she needed before she asked.
blocks.es_reference: El Refrigerador Vacío de Linda: Durante la crisis financiera del 2009, una madre soltera en Ohio llamada Linda perdió su trabajo. Su refrigerador estaba casi vacío. Después de acostar a sus tres hijos se quebrantó en la cocina y oró, Señor, no sé cómo comeremos mañana. Pero Tú prometiste cuidarnos. Confío en Ti. A la mañana siguiente una amiga de la iglesia tocó la puerta con bolsas de víveres. La amiga dijo, No pude dormir anoche — sentí que Dios me decía que necesitabas esto. El testimonio de Linda después no fue sobre la comida; fue que Dios ya sabía lo que ella necesitaba antes de pedírselo.

blocks.en: This is what Matthew 6 looks like on a Wednesday night with no money. Worry tells the disciple to lie awake calculating disasters that have not happened. Trust tells the disciple to surrender the calculation to a Father who has counted hairs on heads and watches sparrows fall. The practical exchange the radical disciple learns to make is a small one and a hard one: replace what if with even if. What if the paycheck does not come becomes even if the paycheck does not come, the Father knows. What if the diagnosis is bad becomes even if the diagnosis is bad, the Father is in the room. The grammar changes; the heart follows.
blocks.es_reference: Esto es cómo se ve Mateo 6 un miércoles por la noche sin dinero. La preocupación le dice al discípulo que se quede despierto calculando desastres que no han ocurrido. La confianza le dice al discípulo que entregue el cálculo a un Padre que ha contado cabellos en cabezas y mira caer pajarillos. El intercambio práctico que el discípulo radical aprende a hacer es uno pequeño y uno duro: reemplazar ¿y si? por aun si. ¿Y si no viene el sueldo se vuelve aun si no viene el sueldo, el Padre lo sabe. ¿Y si el diagnóstico es malo se vuelve aun si el diagnóstico es malo, el Padre está en el cuarto. La gramática cambia; el corazón sigue.

blocks.en: 3. The Lord of Sight
blocks.es_reference: 3. El Señor de la Vista

blocks.en: Hebrews 11:8-10 (NKJV) — abridged: "By faith Abraham obeyed when he was called to go out to the place which he would receive as an inheritance. And he went out, not knowing where he was going. By faith he dwelt in the land of promise as in a foreign country, dwelling in tents with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise; for he waited for the city which has foundations, whose builder and maker is God."
blocks.es_reference: Hebreos 11:8-10 (RVG) — abreviado: "Por fe Abraham, siendo llamado, obedeció para salir al lugar que había de recibir por herencia; y salió sin saber a dónde iba. Por fe habitó en la tierra prometida como en tierra ajena, morando en tabernáculos con Isaac y Jacob, herederos juntamente de la misma promesa; porque esperaba la ciudad que tiene fundamentos, cuyo arquitecto y hacedor es Dios."

blocks.en: Hebrews 11 is the Bible's hall of witnesses for trust that has no immediate evidence. Abraham is the first name on the wall. The summary of his obedience is six words: he went out, not knowing. God had told him where he was going in only the vaguest terms — a land that I will show you — and Abraham packed up the household and started walking. He spent the rest of his life in tents, in a country that was not his, with promises that mostly outlived him. The son finally arrived in Abraham's old age; the nation took another four hundred years; the land took longer than that; the city whose builder and maker is God has not yet come down. Abraham believed it would. He died believing it without seeing it.
blocks.es_reference: Hebreos 11 es el salón de testigos de la Biblia para la confianza que no tiene evidencia inmediata. Abraham es el primer nombre en la pared. El resumen de su obediencia es seis palabras: salió sin saber a dónde iba. Dios le había dicho a dónde iba solo en los términos más vagos — una tierra que te mostraré — y Abraham empacó la casa y comenzó a caminar. Pasó el resto de su vida en tiendas, en un país que no era el suyo, con promesas que mayormente lo sobrevivieron. El hijo finalmente llegó en la vejez de Abraham; la nación tomó otros cuatrocientos años; la tierra tomó más tiempo que eso; la ciudad cuyo arquitecto y hacedor es Dios aún no ha descendido. Abraham creyó que lo haría. Murió creyéndolo sin verlo.

blocks.en: Paul puts the same principle into one verse for the Corinthian church: we walk by faith, not by sight (2 Cor 5:7). This is the third place radical trust gets stretched — not in the dramatic storm and not in the daily worry, but in the long slow obedience in a direction whose endpoint the disciple may never see. Most Christian lives are mostly this. The pastor who plants a church that does not flourish in his lifetime, the parent who prays for a child's salvation for thirty years, the missionary who buries a wife in foreign soil before the first convert is baptized — these are the Abrahams. The future is not visible. It is only promised. The disciple decides which of those is more reliable.
blocks.es_reference: Pablo pone el mismo principio en un versículo para la iglesia de Corinto: por fe andamos, no por vista (2 Cor 5:7). Este es el tercer lugar donde la confianza radical se estira — no en la tormenta dramática y no en la preocupación diaria, sino en la larga y lenta obediencia en una dirección cuyo punto final el discípulo puede que nunca vea. La mayoría de las vidas cristianas son mayormente esto. El pastor que planta una iglesia que no florece en su vida, el padre que ora por la salvación de un hijo por treinta años, el misionero que entierra a una esposa en suelo extranjero antes de que el primer converso sea bautizado — estos son los Abrahams. El futuro no es visible. Solo es prometido. El discípulo decide cuál de esos es más confiable.

blocks.en: Adoniram Judson: In 1812 Adoniram and Ann Judson sailed for Burma, among the first American missionaries sent abroad. The work was painful and slow. Seven years passed before the first convert was baptized. Adoniram was shackled in a filthy prison for nearly two years during a war. They buried children. Ann's health gave out and she died young. From the outside, the mission looked like failure. Judson wrote in one of his darkest hours: the future is as bright as the promises of God. Today more than four million Christians in Myanmar trace their spiritual heritage to the Judsons.
blocks.es_reference: Adoniram Judson: En 1812 Adoniram y Ann Judson zarparon hacia Birmania, entre los primeros misioneros estadounidenses enviados al extranjero. La obra fue dolorosa y lenta. Pasaron siete años antes de que el primer converso fuera bautizado. Adoniram fue encadenado en una prisión sucia por casi dos años durante una guerra. Enterraron hijos. La salud de Ann se quebró y murió joven. Desde afuera, la misión parecía un fracaso. Judson escribió en una de sus horas más oscuras: el futuro es tan brillante como las promesas de Dios. Hoy más de cuatro millones de cristianos en Myanmar trazan su herencia espiritual a los Judsons.

blocks.en: The disciple who walks by sight will not make it through that kind of work. The disciple who walks by faith will. The promises of God do not depend on what is currently visible; they depend on the character of the One who made them. This is why Hebrews defines faith as the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen (Heb 11:1). It is substance even before it is sight. It is evidence even before it is delivery. The radical disciple's sight reaches farther than his eyes do, because his eyes are looking at what God has said and not at what the circumstance is showing.
blocks.es_reference: El discípulo que camina por vista no lo logrará en esa clase de obra. El discípulo que camina por fe sí. Las promesas de Dios no dependen de lo que es actualmente visible; dependen del carácter de Aquel que las hizo. Por esto Hebreos define la fe como la sustancia de las cosas que se esperan, la evidencia de las cosas que no se ven (Heb 11:1). Es sustancia aun antes de ser vista. Es evidencia aun antes de la entrega. La vista del discípulo radical alcanza más lejos que sus ojos, porque sus ojos están mirando lo que Dios ha dicho y no lo que la circunstancia está mostrando.

blocks.en: Storms, worries, and unseen futures are the three places trust gets stretched. The old wineskin of self-reliance cracks at every one of them. The new wineskin of faith holds. The Lord of the storm is in your boat. The Lord over worry is your Father. The Lord of sight has spoken the future already, and His Word does not return void. Where do you need radical trust today? In your storm, your worry, or your unseen tomorrow? Stretch.
blocks.es_reference: Las tormentas, las preocupaciones, y los futuros no vistos son los tres lugares donde la confianza se estira. El odre viejo de la autosuficiencia se agrieta en cada uno de ellos. El odre nuevo de la fe sostiene. El Señor de la tormenta está en tu barca. El Señor sobre la preocupación es tu Padre. El Señor de la vista ya ha hablado el futuro, y Su Palabra no vuelve vacía. ¿Dónde necesitas confianza radical hoy? ¿En tu tormenta, tu preocupación, o tu mañana no visto? Estírate.

options: A. A first-century recipe for fermented drinkA. Una receta del primer siglo para bebida fermentada
B. The radical life Jesus brings — new wine that requires stretchable new wineskins of faithB. La vida radical que Jesús trae — vino nuevo que requiere odres nuevos elásticos de fe
C. The need to abandon all Old Testament teachingC. La necesidad de abandonar toda enseñanza del Antiguo Testamento
D. The difference between Jews and GentilesD. La diferencia entre judíos y gentiles
mc.why: Correct. Jesus calls His disciples into a faith that stretches beyond what feels safe — the kind of trust that does not collapse under storms, worries, or uncertainty. Old, brittle wineskins of self-reliance burst under the pressure of new life; new, flexible wineskins of faith hold.Correcto. Jesús llama a Sus discípulos a una fe que se estire más allá de lo que se siente seguro — la clase de confianza que no se colapsa bajo tormentas, preocupaciones, o incertidumbre. Los odres viejos y frágiles de la autosuficiencia revientan bajo la presión de la nueva vida; los odres nuevos y flexibles de la fe sostienen.

mc.stem: 2. The three places radical trust gets stretched, according to this unit, are:2. Los tres lugares donde la confianza radical se estira, según esta unidad, son:
options: A. Money, marriage, ministryA. Dinero, matrimonio, ministerio
B. Past, present, futureB. Pasado, presente, futuro
C. Body, soul, spiritC. Cuerpo, alma, espíritu
D. Over storms, over worry, over what the eye cannot yet seeD. Sobre las tormentas, sobre la preocupación, sobre lo que el ojo aún no puede ver
mc.why: Correct. Storms (great fears), worry (daily small fears), and unseen futures (the long obedience toward what is only promised). These three are where the old wineskin cracks and where the new wineskin must stretch. Each has a different scripture anchor: Mark 4, Matthew 6, and Hebrews 11.Correcto. Las tormentas (grandes temores), la preocupación (pequeños temores diarios), y los futuros no vistos (la larga obediencia hacia lo que solo es prometido). Estos tres son donde el odre viejo se agrieta y donde el odre nuevo debe estirarse. Cada uno tiene un ancla diferente de la Escritura: Marcos 4, Mateo 6, y Hebreos 11.

mc.stem: 3. In Mark 4:37-41, where was Jesus during the storm on the Sea of Galilee?3. En Marcos 4:37-41, ¿dónde estaba Jesús durante la tormenta en el Mar de Galilea?
options: A. On the shore, watching from a distanceA. En la orilla, mirando desde lejos
B. Praying on a mountainB. Orando en un monte
C. Asleep in the stern of the boat with His head on a pillowC. Dormido en la popa de la barca con la cabeza sobre un cabezal
D. Walking on the water toward themD. Caminando sobre las aguas hacia ellos
mc.why: Correct. Asleep in the stern, head on a cushion. The disciples were not crossing alone; the Lord of the storm was in the boat with them. The detail of His sleeping is not incidental — it shows complete confidence in His own authority over what was scaring His professional-fisherman friends.Correcto. Dormido en la popa, cabeza sobre un cabezal. Los discípulos no cruzaban solos; el Señor de la tormenta estaba en la barca con ellos. El detalle de Su dormir no es incidental — muestra completa confianza en Su propia autoridad sobre lo que estaba asustando a Sus amigos pescadores profesionales.

mc.stem: 4. The disciples' question to Jesus during the storm — "Do You not care that we are perishing?" — is described in this unit as:4. La pregunta de los discípulos a Jesús durante la tormenta — "¿No tienes cuidado que perecemos?" — se describe en esta unidad como:
options: A. Half-accusation, half-prayerA. Mitad acusación, mitad oración
B. A confession of sinB. Una confesión de pecado
C. A theological statement about omniscienceC. Una declaración teológica sobre la omnisciencia
D. A request for additional disciplesD. Una petición de discípulos adicionales
mc.why: Correct. Half-accusation, half-prayer — the question every storm eventually draws out of every Christian. The disciples were not wrong to wake Him; they were wrong about whether He cared. The answer is the same Jesus gave them: He cares enough to be in the boat, and has authority enough to make the wind listen.Correcto. Mitad acusación, mitad oración — la pregunta que cada tormenta eventualmente saca de cada cristiano. Los discípulos no estaban equivocados en despertarlo; estaban equivocados sobre si Él tenía cuidado. La respuesta es la misma que Jesús les dio: Él tiene suficiente cuidado para estar en la barca, y tiene suficiente autoridad para hacer que el viento escuche.

mc.stem: 5. According to this unit, the lesson of Mark 4 is NOT that storms will never come. The actual lesson is:5. Según esta unidad, la lección de Marcos 4 NO es que las tormentas nunca vendrán. La lección real es:

La fe no siempre detiene la tormenta, pero ancla al discípulo al Salvador que la gobierna. Las tormentas están garantizadas; el abandono no.

mc.stem: 6. After Jesus stilled the storm, this unit says the disciples now had something larger to fear because:6. Después de que Jesús calmó la tormenta, esta unidad dice que los discípulos ahora tenían algo más grande que temer porque:

mc.why: Correct. The men who had been afraid of the storm now had something larger to be afraid of, because the One in the boat with them commanded weather. They "feared exceedingly" — not the wind, which had just stopped, but Jesus, who had just stopped it. Recognition of authority always reframes the fear.Correcto. Los hombres que habían tenido miedo de la tormenta ahora tenían algo más grande de qué tener miedo, porque Aquel que estaba en la barca con ellos mandaba el clima. "Temieron con gran temor" — no al viento, que acababa de detenerse, sino a Jesús, quien acababa de detenerlo. El reconocimiento de la autoridad siempre reencuadra el temor.

mc.stem: 7. The Elisabeth Elliot illustration describes her response to the 1956 killing of her husband and four other missionaries by the Huaorani as:7. La ilustración de Elisabeth Elliot describe su respuesta a la matanza en 1956 de su esposo y otros cuatro misioneros por los Huaorani como:
options: A. Returning home to America permanentlyA. Regresar a casa a Estados Unidos permanentemente

Dos años después de que su esposo Jim fue muerto, Elisabeth — veintinueve años, con una bebé — fue a vivir entre los Huaorani. Muchos vinieron a la fe, incluyendo algunos de los hombres que habían blandido las lanzas. El mismo Jesús que calmó el Mar de Galilea aún gobierna sobre las tormentas más feroces de la vida.

mc.stem: 8. In Matthew 6:25-27, Jesus uses two ordinary things to argue against worry. They are:8. En Mateo 6:25-27, Jesús usa dos cosas ordinarias para argumentar contra la preocupación. Ellas son:
options: A. Birds of the air and lilies of the fieldA. Las aves del cielo y los lirios del campo

mc.why: Correct. Birds and lilies. Birds do not run agribusiness, have no granaries, and the Father feeds them. Lilies do not weave fabric, have no looms, and Solomon was not as well dressed as one of them. The argument is not that food and clothing do not matter; the argument is that they matter to the Father.Correcto. Aves y lirios. Las aves no manejan agronegocios, no tienen graneros, y el Padre las alimenta. Los lirios no tejen telas, no tienen telares, y Salomón no estaba tan bien vestido como uno de ellos. El argumento no es que la comida y la ropa no importan; el argumento es que le importan al Padre.

mc.stem: 9. According to this unit, what does worry actually do?9. Según esta unidad, ¿qué hace realmente la preocupación?
options: A. Lengthens lifeA. Alarga la vida
B. Demonstrates faithB. Demuestra fe
C. Pleases God when it concerns serious mattersC. Agrada a Dios cuando concierne a asuntos serios
D. Impersonates prayer while accomplishing none of prayer's workD. Imita la oración mientras no logra nada del trabajo de la oración
mc.why: Correct. Worry feels like spiritual labor but produces only fatigue. It has never lengthened a life, paid a bill, healed a child, or restored a marriage. Jesus' rhetorical question in v. 27 — "which of you by worrying can add one cubit to his stature?" — has only one honest answer: none.Correcto. La preocupación se siente como labor espiritual pero produce solo fatiga. Nunca ha alargado una vida, pagado una cuenta, sanado a un niño, o restaurado un matrimonio. La pregunta retórica de Jesús en el v. 27 — "¿quién de vosotros podrá, por mucho que se afane, añadir a su estatura un codo?" — tiene solo una respuesta honesta: ninguno.

mc.stem: 10. Matthew 6:33 names the alternative to worry. It is:10. Mateo 6:33 nombra la alternativa a la preocupación. Es:
options: A. Seeking first the kingdom of God and His righteousnessA. Buscar primeramente el reino de Dios y su justicia

mc.why: Correct. Seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things shall be added to you. The order matters. The kingdom is first; the needs come after. Reverse the order and even the needs do not get met properly. The promise is not "all these things" first and "the kingdom" later; it is exactly the reverse.Correcto. Buscad primeramente el reino de Dios y su justicia, y todas estas cosas os serán añadidas. El orden importa. El reino es primero; las necesidades vienen después. Invierte el orden y aun las necesidades no son satisfechas apropiadamente. La promesa no es "todas estas cosas" primero y "el reino" después; es exactamente lo contrario.

mc.stem: 11. The Linda illustration describes a single mother in Ohio in 2009 who:11. La ilustración de Linda describe a una madre soltera en Ohio en el 2009 que:

B. Lost her job, had a nearly empty refrigerator, prayed in surrender, and received groceries the next morning from a friend who said she could not sleepB. Perdió su trabajo, tenía un refrigerador casi vacío, oró en rendición, y recibió víveres a la mañana siguiente de una amiga que dijo no haber podido dormir

After tucking the children into bed she prayed in surrender: "Lord, I don't know how we'll eat tomorrow. But You promised to care for us. I trust You." Linda's testimony was not the food; it was that God already knew before she asked.Correcto. Linda tenía tres hijos, un refrigerador casi vacío, y ninguna idea de cómo comerían. Después de acostar a los niños oró en rendición: "Señor, no sé cómo comeremos mañana. Pero Tú prometiste cuidarnos. Confío en Ti." A la mañana siguiente una amiga llegó con víveres, diciendo que no había podido dormir — Dios le había dicho que Linda necesitaba esto. mc.stem: 12. The "small and hard" grammatical exchange this unit teaches the disciple to make is:12. El intercambio gramatical "pequeño y duro" que esta unidad enseña al discípulo a hacer es:
options: A. Replace "I" with "we"A. Reemplazar "yo" con "nosotros"
B. Replace "what if" with "even if"B. Reemplazar "¿y si?" con "aun si"

"What if the diagnosis is bad" becomes "even if the diagnosis is bad, the Father is in the room." The grammar changes; the heart follows. Worry lives in "what if"; trust lives in "even if."Correcto. "¿Y si no viene el sueldo?" se vuelve "aun si no viene el sueldo, el Padre lo sabe." "¿Y si el diagnóstico es malo?" se vuelve "aun si el diagnóstico es malo, el Padre está en el cuarto." La gramática cambia; el corazón sigue. La preocupación vive en "¿y si?"; la confianza vive en "aun si."

mc.stem: 13. Hebrews 11:8 summarizes Abraham's obedience in six words. They are:13. Hebreos 11:8 resume la obediencia de Abraham en seis palabras. Ellas son:
options: A. He kept his eyes on JesusA. Mantuvo sus ojos en Jesús

This is the third stretch of trust: the long obedience without immediate evidence.Correcto. "Salió sin saber a dónde iba." Dios le había dicho solo "una tierra que te mostraré," y Abraham empacó la casa y comenzó a caminar. Pasó el resto de su vida en tiendas, en un país que no era el suyo, con promesas que mayormente lo sobrevivieron. Este es el tercer estiramiento de la confianza: la larga obediencia sin evidencia inmediata.

mc.stem: 14. Paul's one-verse summary of the same principle, given to the Corinthian church, is:14. El resumen de un versículo de Pablo del mismo principio, dado a la iglesia de Corinto, es:

B. "All things work together for good" (Rom 8:28)B. "Todas las cosas obran para bien" (Rom 8:28)
C. "I can do all things through Christ" (Phil 4:13)C. "Todo lo puedo en Cristo" (Fil 4:13)
D. "Be anxious for nothing" (Phil 4:6)D. "Por nada estéis afanosos" (Fil 4:6)
mc.why: Correct. 2 Corinthians 5:7 — "we walk by faith, not by sight." Paul condenses the Abraham principle into a single verse: the disciple's sight reaches farther than his eyes do, because his eyes look at what God has said and not at what the circumstance is showing. The destination is reliable because the One who described it does not lie.Correcto. 2 Corintios 5:7 — "por fe andamos, no por vista." Pablo condensa el principio de Abraham en un solo versículo: la vista del discípulo alcanza más lejos que sus ojos, porque sus ojos miran lo que Dios ha dicho y no lo que la circunstancia está mostrando. El destino es confiable porque Aquel que lo describió no miente.

mc.stem: 15. Adoniram Judson's famous statement, written in one of his darkest hours, was:15. La famosa declaración de Adoniram Judson, escrita en una de sus horas más oscuras, fue:

Judson's seven years before the first convert, his nearly two years in a filthy prison, his buried children, and Ann's young death by collapse of health — none of it shook the underlying conviction: the future is as bright as the promises of God. Today more than four million Christians in Myanmar trace their spiritual heritage to him.Correcto. Los siete años de Judson antes del primer converso, sus casi dos años en una prisión sucia, sus hijos enterrados, y la muerte temprana de Ann por el colapso de la salud — nada de ello sacudió la convicción subyacente: el futuro es tan brillante como las promesas de Dios. Hoy más de cuatro millones de cristianos en Myanmar trazan su herencia espiritual a él.

mc.stem: 16. Hebrews 11:1 defines faith as:16. Hebreos 11:1 define la fe como:
options: A. The absence of doubtA. La ausencia de la duda
B. The feeling of certaintyB. El sentimiento de certeza

D. The substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seenD. La sustancia de las cosas que se esperan, la evidencia de las cosas que no se ven
mc.why: Correct. Hebrews 11:1 — faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen. It is substance even before it is sight. It is evidence even before it is delivery. The radical disciple has substantial possessions and convincing evidence that the rest of the world cannot see because faith treats what God said as real.Correcto. Hebreos 11:1 — la fe es la sustancia de las cosas que se esperan, la evidencia de las cosas que no se ven. Es sustancia aun antes de ser vista. Es evidencia aun antes de la entrega. El discípulo radical tiene posesiones sustanciales y evidencia convincente que el resto del mundo no puede ver porque la fe trata como real lo que Dios dijo.

mc.stem: 17. The unit names three categories of disciple who exemplify the "long, slow obedience without seeing the endpoint":17. La unidad nombra tres categorías de discípulos que ejemplifican la "larga y lenta obediencia sin ver el punto final":

D. The pastor whose church does not flourish in his lifetime, the parent who prays for a child for thirty years, the missionary who buries a wife before the first convert is baptizedD. El pastor cuya iglesia no florece en su vida, el padre que ora por un hijo por treinta años, el misionero que entierra a una esposa antes del primer converso bautizado
mc.why: Correct. These are "the Abrahams" — ordinary disciples in long obedience whose endpoint they will not personally see. Most Christian lives are mostly this. Estos son "los Abrahams" — discípulos ordinarios en larga obediencia cuyo punto final ellos no verán personalmente. La mayoría de las vidas cristianas son mayormente esto. mc.stem: 18. According to the unit, the promises of God do not depend on what is currently visible. They depend on:18. Según la unidad, las promesas de Dios no dependen de lo que es actualmente visible. Dependen de:
options: A. The strength of the disciple's faithA. La fuerza de la fe del discípulo
B. The character of the One who made themB. El carácter de Aquel que las hizo
C. The political climate of the ageC. El clima político de la época
D. The unity of the churchD. La unidad de la iglesia
mc.why: Correct. The character of the One who made them. God's faithfulness is the substance behind every promise — the disciple's faith does not generate the promise's reliability, it receives it. Even the weakest faith holds onto the strongest God; even the strongest faith without a faithful God would hold nothing. The reliability is on His side, not ours.Correcto. El carácter de Aquel que las hizo. La fidelidad de Dios es la sustancia detrás de cada promesa — la fe del discípulo no genera la confiabilidad de la promesa, la recibe. Aun la fe más débil se aferra al Dios más fuerte; aun la fe más fuerte sin un Dios fiel no sostendría nada. La confiabilidad está de Su lado, no del nuestro.

mc.stem: 19. The unit's final image is that the old wineskin of self-reliance cracks at all three stress-tests, while:19. La imagen final de la unidad es que el odre viejo de la autosuficiencia se agrieta en los tres exámenes de tensión, mientras que:
options: A. The new wineskin of religious observance contains the wineA. El odre nuevo de la observancia religiosa contiene el vino
B. The new wineskin of human effort holdsB. El odre nuevo del esfuerzo humano sostiene
C. The new wineskin of faith holdsC. El odre nuevo de la fe sostiene
D. The new wineskin of clear circumstances holdsD. El odre nuevo de las circunstancias claras sostiene
mc.why: Correct. The new wineskin of faith holds. Storms cannot break it because the Lord of the storm is in the boat. Worry cannot puncture it because the Father already knows what is needed. Unseen futures cannot collapse it because the promises of God are as reliable as His character. Only faith stretches to hold all three at once.Correcto. El odre nuevo de la fe sostiene. Las tormentas no pueden romperlo porque el Señor de la tormenta está en la barca. La preocupación no puede pincharlo porque el Padre ya sabe lo que se necesita. Los futuros no vistos no pueden colapsarlo porque las promesas de Dios son tan confiables como Su carácter. Solo la fe se estira para sostener los tres a la vez.

mc.stem: 20. The closing application question of the unit is:20. La pregunta de aplicación de cierre de la unidad es:
options: A. Have you memorized enough Scripture?A. ¿Has memorizado suficiente Escritura?
B. Have you attended enough church services?B. ¿Has asistido a suficientes cultos?
C. Have you given enough offerings?C. ¿Has dado suficientes ofrendas?
D. Where do you need radical trust today — in your storm, your worry, or your unseen tomorrow?D. ¿Dónde necesitas confianza radical hoy — en tu tormenta, tu preocupación, o tu mañana no visto?
mc.why: Correct. Where do you need radical trust today — in your storm, your worry, or your unseen tomorrow? Stretch. The closing word is one syllable: stretch. The new wineskin is built for stretching. Refusing to stretch is what kills old wineskins; choosing to stretch is what proves the new one is alive.Correcto. ¿Dónde necesitas confianza radical hoy — en tu tormenta, tu preocupación, o tu mañana no visto? Estírate. La palabra de cierre es una sílaba: estírate. El odre nuevo está hecho para estirarse. Rehusar estirarse es lo que mata a los odres viejos; escoger estirarse es lo que prueba que el nuevo está vivo.

When the storm comes, the disciple's first response is not panic but ____: speaking to the Lord who is in the boat.

sa.prompt: Explain the wineskins image (Luke 5:37-38) as the unit uses it. Why is self-reliance an 'old, brittle' wineskin, and what does the 'new wineskin of faith' actually have to do?
sa.model: New wine ferments and expands; old, brittle wineskins burst under the pressure of new life. Self-reliance is the old wineskin: it has no give, no flexibility, no room for what God is now doing. When storms, worry, or unseen futures put pressure on a self-reliant disciple, the disciple cracks because there is no room to stretch. The new wineskin of faith does the opposite — it stretches to hold what God is pouring in. Faith's job is not to generate the new wine; faith's job is to be elastic enough not to burst when the new wine arrives.

sa.prompt: Walk through Mark 4:37-41. Where was Jesus during the storm, what did the disciples ask Him, what did He do, and what fear replaced their fear of the storm?
sa.model: Jesus was asleep in the stern of the boat, head on a pillow. The disciples — several of them professional fishermen — were terrified by the storm and woke Him with a question that was half-accusation and half-prayer: 'Teacher, do You not care that we are perishing?' Jesus arose, rebuked the wind, and said three words to the sea: 'Peace, be still!' The wind ceased; a great calm followed. The disciples 'feared exceedingly' — not the storm, which had just stopped, but the One who had stopped it. Their fear was transferred from the weather to the authority that commanded the weather: 'Who can this be, that even the wind and the sea obey Him?'

sa.prompt: Why does this unit insist that 'the Lord of the storm is in the boat with you' rather than promising that storms will not come? How does that change the disciple's posture when storms arrive?
sa.model: Storms are guaranteed; abandonment is not. The unit refuses the soft promise that faith exempts the disciple from weather, because that promise is not biblical and would collapse the first time it failed. The harder and more truthful promise is presence — the Lord of the storm is in the boat. This changes posture in three ways. (1) The disciple's first response is prayer, not panic — 'Jesus is in my boat' replaces 'I am alone in this.' (2) The disciple can rest, because the One sleeping on the cushion is the One who made the wind. (3) The disciple accepts that Jesus may calm the storm, may calm it later, or may carry the disciple through the middle of it — none of which is a sign that He does not care.

sa.prompt: Summarize Jesus' argument from the birds and lilies (Matthew 6:25-27). What does He prove with these two ordinary examples, and what is His rhetorical question in v. 27?
sa.model: Jesus points to two ordinary things right in front of His listeners. Birds do not run agribusiness, have no granaries, do not sow or reap; the Father feeds them anyway. Lilies do not weave fabric, have no looms, do not labor or spin; Solomon in his full royal wardrobe was not as well dressed as the wildflower that comes up in three weeks and is gone in six. The argument is not that food and clothing do not matter; the argument is that they matter to the Father, who is already providing for creatures less valuable than His disciples. His rhetorical question in v. 27 — 'Which of you by worrying can add one cubit to his stature?' — has only one honest answer: none. Worry produces no measurable result; it only produces fatigue.

sa.prompt: Explain the 'what if' to 'even if' grammatical exchange that the unit teaches. Give two concrete examples of how the same situation reads differently in each grammar.
sa.model: Worry lives in 'what if'; trust lives in 'even if.' The unit's two concrete examples: (1) 'What if the paycheck does not come' becomes 'even if the paycheck does not come, the Father knows.' (2) 'What if the diagnosis is bad' becomes 'even if the diagnosis is bad, the Father is in the room.' The grammar changes; the heart follows. 'What if' calculates disasters that have not happened and may never happen, generating fatigue without any actual progress. 'Even if' surrenders the disaster — present or future, real or imagined — to a Father who has already counted hairs on heads and watches sparrows fall. Same syllables, different theology. The exchange is small enough to make on any given Wednesday, and hard enough to be a real act of faith every time.

sa.prompt: Tell the story of Linda's empty fridge. Why does the unit say her testimony afterward was not really about the food?
sa.model: During the 2009 financial crisis, Linda — a single mother in Ohio with three children — lost her job. Her refrigerator was nearly empty and she had no idea how they would eat the next day. After tucking the children into bed she broke down in the kitchen and prayed in surrender: 'Lord, I don't know how we'll eat tomorrow. But You promised to care for us. I trust You.' The next morning a friend from church arrived at the door with bags of groceries, saying she could not sleep the previous night — she felt God telling her Linda needed this. Linda's testimony afterward was not the food (which was real and welcome). Her testimony was that God already knew what she needed before she asked, and was already moving on her friend's heart while Linda was still calculating disasters in her kitchen. The story illustrates Matthew 6 in real time: the Father feeds His own.

sa.prompt: Hebrews 11:8 says Abraham 'went out, not knowing where he was going.' Describe what Abraham's life looked like after that obedience, and why he is the model for the disciple who trusts what cannot yet be seen.
sa.model: God told Abraham in only the vaguest terms — 'a land that I will show you' — and Abraham packed up the household and started walking. He spent the rest of his life in tents, in a country that was not his, with promises that mostly outlived him. The son finally arrived in Abraham's old age; the nation took another four hundred years; the land took longer than that; the city 'whose builder and maker is God' has not yet come down. Abraham believed it would. He died believing it without seeing it. He is the model for the disciple who trusts the unseen because his obedience showed that the most reliable thing about a future is not the visible map but the character of the One who described the destination. Hebrews 11 puts his name first on the wall of witnesses for that reason.

sa.prompt: The unit names three ordinary categories of disciple as 'the Abrahams' — disciples in long obedience whose endpoint they will not personally see. List the three and explain why their faithfulness rests on the character of God rather than on visible results.
sa.model: The three: (1) The pastor who plants a church that does not flourish in his lifetime. (2) The parent who prays for a child's salvation for thirty years. (3) The missionary who buries a wife in foreign soil before the first convert is baptized. These are the Abrahams. The future is not visible to them; it is only promised. Their faithfulness cannot rest on visible returns within their lifespan because there are no visible returns within their lifespan — and yet they keep going. The only available foundation is the character of the One making the promises. God's faithfulness does not depend on the disciple seeing results; the disciple's faithfulness depends on God's character being what He says it is. Most Christian lives are mostly this third category, and most spiritual fruit ripens after the planter is buried.

sa.prompt: Tell the story of Adoniram Judson and explain his statement 'the future is as bright as the promises of God.' What did he not see in his lifetime, and what came from his faithfulness?
sa.model: Adoniram and Ann Judson sailed for Burma in 1812 as among the first American missionaries sent abroad. The work was painful and slow: seven years passed before the first convert was baptized; Adoniram was shackled in a filthy prison for nearly two years during a war; they buried children; Ann's health gave out and she died young. From the outside the mission looked like failure. From the inside, Judson wrote during one of his darkest hours: 'the future is as bright as the promises of God.' That sentence does not depend on visible evidence; it depends on Whose character stands behind the promise. Judson did not see the result in his lifetime. Today more than four million Christians in Myanmar trace their spiritual heritage to the Judsons. The brightness was real all along; it just was not yet visible to the one trusting it.

sa.prompt: Synthesize the unit's central argument: storms, worry, and unseen futures are the three places trust stretches. What is the old wineskin that cracks at each one, what is the new wineskin that holds, and what is the closing personal application the unit asks of the disciple?
sa.model: Storms, worries, and unseen futures are the three stress-tests of faith. At each one the old wineskin of self-reliance cracks: it cannot calm a sea, it cannot calculate a future into existence, it cannot manufacture certainty about what God has not yet shown. The new wineskin of faith stretches and holds at each one for a different reason. In storms, faith holds because the Lord of the storm is in the boat. In worry, faith holds because the Father already knows what is needed before the disciple asks. In unseen futures, faith holds because the promises of God are as reliable as His character. The closing application is direct and personal: 'Where do you need radical trust today — in your storm, your worry, or your unseen tomorrow?' The unit ends with one word: stretch. Refusing to stretch is what kills old wineskins; choosing to stretch is what proves the new one is alive.
